questions.text: Which evidenced user outcome and constraint justify this change, and which premise would invalidate it?
Which materially simpler user experience alternatives were considered against the same evidence?
Are entry, success, empty, loading, partial, denied, failure, recovery, and return states explicitly covered?
Does the experience preserve user intent and understandable state across retries, navigation, and interruption?
Are keyboard, focus, semantics, contrast, motion, zoom, error identification, and assistive-technology behavior evidenced?
Are labels, instructions, errors, and recovery actions specific, consistent, and usable without hidden context?
Which representative workflows and user-impact signals validate the experience without substituting opinion for observation?
Which baseline experience behavior could regress, and what evidence detects it?
